items.ask: Out of every 100 Americans, how many are transgender?
items.note: Self-ID has risen since 2022 and estimates range ~0.5-1.6%. Cite the year.

items.ask: Out of every 100 Americans, how many are Muslim?
Out of every 100 Americans, how many are Jewish?
Out of every 100 Americans, how many are gay or lesbian?
Out of every 100 Americans, how many are bisexual?
Out of every 100 Americans, how many are Native American?
Out of every 100 Americans, how many are Asian American?
Out of every 100 Americans, how many are Black?
Out of every 100 Americans, how many are left-handed?
items.note: THE KEY CONTROL ITEM. Nothing political about handedness and people are still badly wrong. Proves the effect is cognitive, not partisan. Actual is cited as 10-12%.

items.ask: Out of every 100 Americans, how many are Christian?
items.note: Underestimate. Large groups get shrunk.

items.ask: Out of every 100 Americans, how many finished high school?
Out of every 100 American adults, how many are married?
items.note: Nearly right. Groups near 50% are estimated well. This is the item that proves the pattern is compression toward the middle rather than general innumeracy.

items.ask: Out of every 100 American adults, how many have at least one child?
items.note: Almost exact. Same reason as 'married'.

items.ask: Out of every 100 Republicans, how many agree that properly controlled immigration can be good for America?
items.note: Largest Democratic gap: 33 points. Independents guessed 65%.

items.ask: Out of every 100 Republicans, how many agree that racism still exists in America?
items.note: Gap 28. Independents 56%.

items.ask: Out of every 100 Republicans, how many agree that many Muslims are good Americans?
items.note: Gap 29. Independents 47%.

items.ask: Out of every 100 Republicans, how many agree that sexism still exists in America?
Out of every 100 Republicans, how many agree the government should do more to keep guns from bad people?
Out of every 100 Republicans, how many agree that Donald Trump is a flawed person?
items.note: Gap of -1. Democrats nailed this one. Good palate cleanser — the gap is not universal.

items.ask: Out of every 100 Republicans, how many agree people are right to be concerned about climate change?
items.note: Gap of -2. Also accurate.

items.ask: Out of every 100 Democrats, how many DISAGREE that most police are bad people?
items.note: Largest gap in the whole study: 37 points. Independents 54%.

items.ask: Out of every 100 Democrats, how many are proud to be American while acknowledging the country's flaws?
Out of every 100 Democrats, how many agree it is important that men are protected from false accusations of sexual assault?
Out of every 100 Democrats, how many DISAGREE that the US should have completely open borders?
items.note: Gap 33. Pairs with mic-immigration: each side thinks the other is far more extreme on immigration than it is.

items.ask: Out of every 100 Democrats, how many agree that law-abiding citizens should have the right to bear firearms?
Out of every 100 Democrats, how many DISAGREE that America should be a socialist country?
Out of every 100 Democrats, how many DISAGREE that the US should abolish ICE?
items.note: Smallest gap in Table 2: 13 points.

items.ask: Out of every 100 Republicans, how many hold views most would call extreme?
Out of every 100 Democrats, how many hold views most would call extreme?
items.note: Republicans imagine nearly twice as many extreme Democrats as exist.

items.ask: Out of every 100 Democrats, how many are Black?
Out of every 100 Democrats, how many belong to a labor union?
Out of every 100 Democrats, how many are gay, lesbian or bisexual?
Out of every 100 Democrats, how many are atheist or agnostic?
Out of every 100 Republicans, how many earn more than $250,000 a year?
items.note: Largest ratio in the set: 17x.

items.ask: Out of every 100 Republicans, how many are evangelical?
Out of every 100 Republicans, how many live in the South?
Out of every 100 Republicans, how many are 65 or older?
Out of every 100 dollars of American household wealth, how many are owned by the richest 1% of households?
items.note: Biggest overestimate of any country on this question: +25 points. Truth from the World Inequality Database.

items.ask: Out of every 100 people living in America, how many were born in another country?
items.note: Exactly double. Truth from UN International Migrant Stock.

items.ask: Out of every 100 Americans, how many are Muslim?
items.note: Ipsos 2024 gets 15%; YouGov 2022 got 27% for the same question. Different wording and mode. Use one or the other, not both.

items.ask: Out of every 100 people in Turkiye, how many are Muslim?
items.note: THE PROOF. Same question, and here people UNDERSHOOT by 27 points. Small groups get inflated, large groups get shrunk. It is compression toward the middle, not anti-minority bias.

items.ask: Out of every 100 people in Indonesia, how many are Muslim?
Out of every 100 people in France, how many are Muslim?
Out of every 100 people in Britain, how many are Muslim?
Out of every 100 people in South Africa, how many are Muslim?
Out of every 100 rupees of Indian household wealth, how many are owned by the richest 1%?
items.note: Largest UNDERestimate on the wealth question: -17 points.

items.ask: Out of every 100 pounds of British household wealth, how many are owned by the richest 1%?
items.note: Largest overestimate on this question: +32.

items.ask: Out of every 100 pesos of Mexican household wealth, how many are owned by the richest 1%?
Out of every 100 people living in Brazil, how many were born in another country?
items.note: 24x. The largest ratio on the immigration question.

items.ask: Out of every 100 people living in Canada, how many were born in another country?
Out of every 100 people living in Singapore, how many were born in another country?
items.note: The only country that undershot on immigration - and it is the country with the highest actual share. Compression again.

items.ask: Out of every 100 people living in New Zealand, how many were born in another country?
items.note: Within 3 points. Another accurate case, and again the truth is near the middle of the range.

items.ask: Out of every 100 American girls aged 15 to 19, how many give birth each year?
items.note: Read off the 2024 summary deck; the original wave year is not stated there. Confirm before publishing.

items.ask: Out of every 100 prisoners, how many are immigrants?
items.note: Country/wave not stated on the summary slide. Confirm before publishing.

items.ask: Out of every 100 people, how many think the homicide rate in their country is higher now than in 2000?
items.note: 59% say higher; majorities in 25 of 30 countries do. Ipsos reports it is actually about the same or lower everywhere except Mexico. CAUTION: their own chart puts the US slightly ABOVE its 2000 rate, so the US is a bad instance of this item. Use the global framing or another country.

queued.note: Real leads, numbers NOT yet verified. Do not publish any of these until the primary source is read.
mines: Gapminder / Factfulness 13-question test. Overall results verified: 2017, 14 countries, 10,000+ respondents, average 2.2 correct of 12 against 4 for random guessing, 15% scored zero. PER-QUESTION percentages are only in the book's appendix (p.267) - not on the website. Someone needs the book.

Ipsos Perils of Perception earlier waves, each a separate deck: 2014 (14 countries), 2015 (33), 2016 (40, incl. homophobia and anti-abortion sentiment), 2017 (38), 2020 (32, causes of death), 2021 (30, environment), 2023 (10, conspiracy belief). The 2020 causes-of-death wave and the 2016 wave are the richest untapped ones.

Our World in Data, 'Does the news reflect what we die from?' - heart disease and cancer are 56% of deaths among 15 causes but 7% of coverage; homicide gets 43x its share, terrorism over 18,000x. Not a guess-vs-reality item as it stands, but pairs perfectly with a 'what kills people' question.
Gallup crime series - ~80% thought crime rose in 2023 when it fell; violent victimisation went 80 per 1,000 (1994) to 19 per 1,000 (2010).
Bobby Duffy, 'The Perils of Perception' (2018) - book-length index of the Ipsos waves.
Ahler & Sood MTurk replications in the same paper (n = 382 / 1,036 / 821) - per-party breakdowns of the same eight items.
PNAS Nexus 2024 ingroup-norm work - people overestimate how much their OWN side dislikes the other. The 'undercounting your own side' direction, and nobody has built it.
